subject: Discovery: Agent-style integration patterns & parallel tool fallbacks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@luminary.health>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@luminary.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Aug 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Agent-style integration patterns & parallel tool fallbacks

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap + recommended next steps so we have a shared baseline for the pilot:

1) Primary goal we heard: build an assistant that can (a) fetch structured patient metadata, (b) call a set of clinical tools (notes search, appointment booking, lookup API), and (c) use an embeddings-based reranker for situational relevance. Latency SLO: 500ms p95 for common lookups; acceptable tail up to 1s for multi-tool fanout.

2) Integration pattern we recommend for the pilot: "agent orchestration + prioritized parallel tools" — agent decides a small list of candidate tools, Redwood routes calls in parallel where safe, and we cascade to a reranker/embedding pass if results overlap or confidence is low. Key tradeoffs: throughput (parallel calls) vs cost and consistency.

3) Auth / SDK setup: suggest starting with Redwood SDK + API key for the POC. For Dedicated/VPC later, we recommend OIDC + mTLS. We'll provide an SDK quickstart (node/python) and an auth decision doc.

4) Structured output & tool definitions: use a strict tool schema (name, input_schema, output_schema, retry_policy, cost_estimate). We'll share example tool-definition JSON (attached). Keep the output as typed JSON so the agent can deterministically route to reranker or UI renderers.

5) Error handling & fallbacks: default policy = best-effort parallel then single-tool retry + model-only fallback (text-only response) if all tools fail. For critical ops (booking) require transactional confirmation and immediate human handoff.

Attachments: integration-agent-matrix.xlsx (pilot matrix), example-tool-definitions.json

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood to provide SDK quickstart + example tool defs (Jonas, Rishi) — by Mon 8/12
- Luminary to share WT API specs and auth requirements (Alex/Priya) — by Wed 8/14
- Follow-up architecture call to walk the matrix (all) — propose Thu 8/15 10am PT

If that matches your read, we'll start the quickstart repo and a minimal demo harness (local) you can exercise.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 10 Aug 2024 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Agent-style integration patterns & parallel tool fallbacks

Thanks Jonas — this looks good and aligns with our internal priorities. A couple quick clarifications before the follow-up call: 

1) Parallel calls: we like the idea but worried about rate limits on our note-search API. Would Redwood support per-tool throttling / backoff so we don't accidentally DDOS internal services?

2) Reranker: our current embeddings are stored in ElasticSearch; re-ranking call should accept a small candidate set + embeddings vector and return ranked IDs. Can your reranker call be decoupled to just return a score vector so we keep re-ranking inside our infra?

3) Auth: for now we can provide a service account key; for production we will want SAML/OIDC integrations. Also curious about session-scoped keys for end-user access.

We'll get you our API doc & sample credentials by Tue. Thu 10am PT works for the call.

—Alex
Alex Nguyen
Dir. Product, Integrations | Luminary Health
alex@luminary.health

Subject: Re: Discovery: Agent-style integration patterns & parallel tool fallbacks

Alex — good questions. Quick answers and owners (so nothing slips):

- Per-tool throttling/backoff: yes. Redwood routing supports per-tool rate limits and adaptive backoff at the proxy layer. We can include a config block in the example tool-definition schema (max_qps, concurrency_limit, backoff_policy). Owner: Rishi will include defaults.

- Reranker integration: we can support a thin-call pattern where Redwood returns scores only (no reordering) — implementer passes candidate IDs and embeddings; we return score vector. We'll document the payload and signing requirements. Owner: Jonas + Rishi to produce example call.

- Auth: service account key is fine for POC. For session-scoped tokens we recommend short-lived JWTs minted by your auth layer and validated by Redwood via OIDC. We'll map this in the auth decision doc. Owner: Marissa to coordinate with Luminary infra.

Action: Jonas/Rishi to drop the example-tool-definitions.json and a one-page SDK quickstart into the Drive folder before Mon. Sean — can you take point on scheduling Thu 10am PT and draft an agenda?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Discovery: Agent-style integration patterns & parallel tool fallbacks

Folks — attaching a short tech note (pasted below) with concrete patterns we think will minimize rework and match Luminary constraints. I also attached example-tool-definitions.json to the Drive folder.

--- tech note (summary) ---
1) Tool definition schema (recommended minimal):
   - name (string)
   - id (string)
   - input_schema (JSON Schema URI)
   - output_schema (JSON Schema URI)
   - cost_estimate (milliseconds / token)
   - concurrency_policy (parallel | serial | limited)
   - retry_policy (count, backoff)
   - auth_scope (service_account | session_jwt)

2) Execution model:
   - Agent evaluates plan -> returns prioritized tool candidates (N <= 4).
   - Redwood router fans out calls for candidates where concurrency_policy allows.
   - If multiple tools return overlapping result sets, we run an embeddings-based reranker on combined candidates. Option: return score vector only so Luminary applies final ordering.

3) Error handling patterns:
   - soft-fail: tool returns 5xx or timeout -> remove from candidate set and continue.
   - hard-fail: booking/payment endpoint 4xx -> stop and surface explicit error to user + human handoff.
   - degraded response: tool returns partial schema -> annotate with quality_score and let reranker downweight.

4) Latency & batching:
   - For common queries (single-tool), prefer direct call path with prefix/KV caching.
   - For multi-tool queries, parallel fanout is fine but add per-tool concurrency caps and a short aggregation timeout (e.g., 300ms) to bound p95.

5) Security and audit: log tool call ids + request/response hashes (PII redaction) to satisfy compliance.

--- end note ---

I'll add code snippets to the Drive examples (node/python client). Expect the short repo and examples by Monday EOD PT.

-Rishi
